title: Claims
summary: The registered claims (iss, sub, aud, exp, nbf, iat, jti), custom claims, and checking times with clock skew.

steps.title: Registered claims
body: The payload is a JSON object of **claims**. RFC 7519 reserves short names for the common ones:
| Claim | Name | Meaning |
| `iss` | issuer | who made the token: `https://login.example.com` |
| `sub` | subject | who it is about, a stable id: `"user-8812"` (not an email that may change) |
| `aud` | audience | who it is **for**: `"orders-api"`, or an array of them |
| `exp` | expiration time | not valid at or after this moment |
| `nbf` | not before | not valid before this moment |
| `iat` | issued at | when it was made |
| `jti` | JWT id | a unique id for this token, used to detect replays or revoke it |
Times are **NumericDate**: whole seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC (Unix time). In .NET: `DateTimeOffset.FromUnixTimeSeconds(1700000000)` and `now.ToUnixTimeSeconds()`.
Every claim is optional by the spec, but a sane API **requires** `exp`, `iss` and `aud`.

steps.prompt: Match each claim to the question it answers.
pairs: Which service is it meant for?
Which user or client is it about?
When does it stop being valid?
When does it start being valid?

steps.prompt: The Unix time `1700000000` is 14 November 2023, 22:13:20 UTC. What does this print?
steps.explain: NumericDates are plain seconds, so a 15-minute token has `exp - iat == 900`.

steps.title: Custom claims, and reading claims in C#
body: Add your own claims next to the registered ones: `"role": "admin"`, `"scope": "orders:read orders:write"`, `"tenant": "acme"`. To avoid clashing with names others define, public claim names are registered with IANA or made collision-proof with a URL: `"https://example.com/claims/plan": "pro"`. Keep payloads small (they travel on every request) and never put secrets in them.
`System.Text.Json` reads a payload without any classes:
```csharp fragment
using System.Text.Json;
using var doc = JsonDocument.Parse(payloadJson);
JsonElement root = doc.RootElement;
string? sub = root.GetProperty("sub").GetString();
long exp = root.GetProperty("exp").GetInt64();
bool hasNbf = root.TryGetProperty("nbf", out JsonElement nbf);
Watch out for `aud`: it may be a **string** or an **array** of strings. Check `ValueKind`:
```csharp fragment
var aud = root.GetProperty("aud");
bool ok = aud.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.String
? aud.GetString() == "orders-api"
: aud.EnumerateArray().Any(a => a.GetString() == "orders-api");

steps.prompt: Read the claims you need from the payload.
code: bool hasNbf = root.__4__("nbf", out var nbf);
steps.explain: `TryGetProperty` is the safe way to read a claim that may be missing; `GetProperty` throws `KeyNotFoundException` if it is absent.

steps.title: Clocks disagree: skew
body: The server that issued a token and the one checking it have slightly different clocks. Allow a small **clock skew** (also called leeway), typically 30 seconds to 5 minutes:
```text
expired       if  now >= exp + skew
not yet valid if  now <  nbf - skew

Without skew, a token issued "now" by a server whose clock runs 2 seconds fast is rejected as not yet valid. With a huge skew, an expired token keeps working long after it should. Microsoft's JWT handler defaults to **5 minutes**; many teams lower it.
Always pass `now` into your validation code rather than reading the clock inside it. That way tests can check the exact boundaries.

steps.prompt: A token has `exp = 1000`. The validator allows 60 seconds of skew. Which `now` values are accepted?
options: Any `now` at all, since skew disables the check
steps.explain: Skew extends the deadline: `now >= exp + skew` means expired, so up to 1059 is accepted.

steps.title: Check the times
prompt: Write `string CheckTimes(string payloadJson, long now, long skew)` that returns:
- `"not_yet_valid"` when there is an `nbf` and `now < nbf - skew`,
Check in that order. The tests already import `System.Text.Json`.
starter: string CheckTimes(string payloadJson, long now, long skew)
solution: string CheckTimes(string payloadJson, long now, long skew)
if (root.TryGetProperty("nbf", out var nbf) && now < nbf.GetInt64() - skew) return "not_yet_valid";
template: Dojo.Eq("at exp with no skew -> expired", "expired", CheckTimes(P, 2000, 0));
Dojo.Eq("just after exp but inside 60s skew", "ok", CheckTimes(P, 2059, 60));
Dojo.Eq("before nbf but inside skew", "ok", CheckTimes(P, 950, 60));

steps.title: Check the audience
prompt: Write `bool HasAudience(string payloadJson, string expected)` (`System.Text.Json` is imported by the tests):
- `aud` as a string: `true` when it equals `expected` exactly.
- `aud` as an array: `true` when any element equals `expected`.
- missing `aud`, or any other JSON type: `false`.
solution: if (!doc.RootElement.TryGetProperty("aud", out var aud)) return false;
JsonValueKind.Array => aud.EnumerateArray().Any(a => a.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.String && a.GetString() == expected),
hints: Use `TryGetProperty("aud", out var aud)` and switch on `aud.ValueKind`.
template: Dojo.Eq("string aud that matches", true, HasAudience("{\"aud\":\"orders-api\"}", "orders-api"));
Dojo.Eq("string aud that doesn't", false, HasAudience("{\"aud\":\"billing-api\"}", "orders-api"));
Dojo.Eq("aud of the wrong type", false, HasAudience("{\"aud\":42}", "orders-api"));
